purpose: Five static proposed large-screen arcade designs; QR patterns are mockups, not live join codes.

records.name: salle-arcade
records.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Asset type: one high-fidelity full-screen in-game mockup for a projected shared-screen multiplayer hackathon game, wide landscape 16:9 composition. Render the actual game viewport edge to edge, not a photograph of a screen or a webpage presentation. Image 1 is ONLY a character style and palette reference, NOT an edit target: preserve the family of tiny cute human chibi pixel avatars with navy outlines, big hair, squat hoodies, varied skin tones, cyan/hot-pink/yellow/orange/violet clothing. Create a coherent environment matching that precise chunky arcade pixel-art identity. Crisp nearest-neighbor pixels, limited shade steps, no vector illustration or smooth gradients. About 28 small players spread naturally across an open walkable arena; avatars occupy about 4 percent of image height and are clearly readable with plenty of space between them. The whole point is people moving to answer a question with their position, not combat. One small friendly dark pixel robot presenter with a pale visor stands on a modest upper stage, acting as Grok; no invented logo. The only UI copy is one short question across the upper scene: "TU CODES PLUTÔT..." and two answer labels on two clearly different floor areas: "SOLO" and "EN ÉQUIPE". These are example game-question content, not additional dashboard controls. Floor answer areas remain part of one continuous traversable map, separated by neutral open floor, not cards or framed UI panels. Lower right corner has one small unobtrusive white QR square with a dark QR-like pattern, occupying approximately 7 percent of image width, no text below. No header/navigation/sidebar/footer, no dashboard, no menus, no buttons, no round counters, no scoreboards, no health bars, no player name labels, no locator arrows, no chat bubbles, no marketing copy, no large title/logo, no mockup device frame, no border around the image, no watermark. Details concentrate at the room boundary; most of the floor is visually quiet so a crowd remains legible. It must look like a plausible polished indie multiplayer pixel-art GAME SCREEN, not concept painting.
Direction 01: THE ARCADE HALL. Top-down retro social-game indoor lounge, deep ink-blue checker tiles rendered subtly with low contrast, hot-pink and cyan trims on an upper stage, a few arcade cabinets and low sofas lining only the outer perimeter. Main arena is one broad horizontal rectangle. Left voting area outlined cyan with muted dark-teal fill, right voting area outlined hot pink with muted dark-plum fill. Small yellow pixels give wayfinding accents. Minimal environmental clutter and almost no glow. Cozy energetic community arcade, large usable floor.

Direction 05: ARCADE GAME SHOW. Single question at top belongs to the game stage, not to an interface card. Most restrained and instantly readable of the five, but festive 16-bit TV-show energy. Strict navy/cyan/pink/yellow environment palette with avatar colors from reference.
